comments: β numerical validation — Monte Carlo check of the analytical variance
formula for the octonion associator, Fano-triple case.
Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:
single Fano generator"):
A(a, b, c) := ‖[a, b, c]‖²   where [a,b,c] = (a·b)·c − a·(b·c)
Unperturbed: [a,b,c] = 2·e_7, A = 4.
Perturb a_1 → 1 + δ, δ ~ N(0, σ²). The analytical first-order GUM
variance (from the β document, derivation):
Var(A) ≈ 64 σ²                                (TRUTH)
If the current compiler's stepwise scalar-product rule were applied
instead, it would give:
Var_compiler(A) ≈ 16 σ²                       (COMPILER, 4× low)
This test computes the sample variance of A over N = 100,000 Monte
Carlo samples and compares to the TRUTH formula. It does NOT test the
compiler's variance_of() — that requires the full Knowledge<f64>
chain which introduces unrelated complexities (see ζ buffer bug). The
compiler comparison is deferred to a separate test.
Pass criterion: |MC_var − 64σ²| / 64σ² < 0.05 (5% relative error).
If this passes, β's analytical formula is validated empirically. The
remaining claim — that the compiler produces 16σ² — is then a
separate reading-confirmation task.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `epistemic_var_accumulator_slots`. Regression pin for #1535: a mutable local must carry its uncertainty across reassignment, including when it was initialised from an EXPRESSION and when the reassignment happens inside a loop. It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: VAR_ACCUM_OK
description: Regression pin for #1535: a mutable local must carry its uncertainty across reassignment, including when it was initialised from an EXPRESSION and when the reassignment happens inside a loop.
comments: Regression pin for #1535: a mutable local must carry its uncertainty across
reassignment, including when it was initialised from an EXPRESSION and when the
reassignment happens inside a loop.
Two defects sat here, and the second hid behind the first:
1. Assignment REBOUND the local's variance/sens to the RHS's fresh vregs
instead of copying into fixed slots. A rebind is a compile-time map update
and a loop body's IR is emitted once, so every iteration recomputed from
the pre-loop uncertainty and only one iteration's contribution survived.
2. The fix for (1) allocated those slots BEFORE the branches that bind a
declaration's variance from its RHS, so those branches overwrote them.
Only a literal-initialised local escaped, because a literal leaves those
branches nothing to bind.
Truth values below are first-order GUM propagation, computed independently
rather than read off either engine. var(cl) = 1.24^2 = 1.5376.
TEST 1 deliberately uses NO loop. The defect never needed one — a loop only
turned a wrong answer into a catastrophic one. Four loop-based repros failed to
separate the two causes; three straight-line assignments did it immediately.
If this pin ever regresses, TEST 1 is the one that localises it.

description: #1586/#1570: the native_v2 label tier (NC_V2_LABEL_* in self-hosted/native/ frame.sio) was [i64; 256] with BOTH bounds silent -- no else, no sentinel. An `if` lowers to 2 labels + 2 jump patches, so the cap bit at ~128 `if`s in
comments: #1586/#1570: the native_v2 label tier (NC_V2_LABEL_* in self-hosted/native/
frame.sio) was [i64; 256] with BOTH bounds silent -- no else, no sentinel.
An `if` lowers to 2 labels + 2 jump patches, so the cap bit at ~128 `if`s in
ONE function. Past that, nc_add_label_patch dropped the patch and the jz/jmp
rel32 operand stayed at its placeholder 0, so the branch fell through instead
of jumping. The program still exited 0. Measured on a flat chain of N
comparisons, the number of WRONG results was exactly N - 128.
TWO THINGS ABOUT THE SHAPE OF THIS TEST ARE THE TEST.
1. It must all be in ONE function. nc_v2_reset_label_state runs at the top of
every function, so splitting these across helpers gives each a fresh
counter and the bug disappears -- which is exactly why "move it into a
helper function" was the documented workaround on #1570, #1577 and #1586,
and why nothing in the suite caught this.
2. They must be STRAIGHT-LINE `if`s, not a loop. A loop body allocates its
labels once at lowering time no matter how many times it runs, so a
hundred-iteration loop contributes about six labels and proves nothing.
150 independent `if`s => 300 labels, past the old 256 cap and inside the

Gresnigt (EPJC 2019/2024; arXiv:2306.13098) builds three fermion generations from three octonion
subalgebras of the sedenions 𝕊 sharing a common quaternion, cyclically related by the family S₃.
The paper's three copies (its basis, App. A) are, as index sets:
sharing the quaternion ℍ = ⟨e₄,e₈,e₁₂⟩ = {4,8,12}.
This test certifies, in this repo's Cayley-Dickson convention:
(a) each 𝕆_i is a genuine (zero-divisor-free) octonion, all three ambient-equivalent (each has 6
non-anticommuting internal left-mult pairs in the 16-dim Cℓ(8));  ℍ = 𝕆₁∩𝕆₂∩𝕆₃ = {4,8,12};
(b) the pure 3-cycle φ = (e₁e₂e₃)(e₅e₆e₇)(e₉e₁₀e₁₁)(e₁₃e₁₄e₁₅) [all signs +1, fixing e₀,e₄,e₈,e₁₂]
is a genuine algebra automorphism of 𝕊 (all 256 products), of order 3, cyclically permuting
𝕆₁→𝕆₂→𝕆₃ and fixing ℍ and e₈;
(c) φ = g ⊕ g is DIAGONAL under 𝕊 = 𝕆 ⊕ 𝕆·e₈ with g = (e₁e₂e₃)(e₅e₆e₇) an automorphism of the base
octonion {e₁..e₇} — so φ ∈ G₂ = Aut(𝕆).
HONEST BOUNDARY (this is NOT a physics bridge). Because φ ∈ G₂ and G₂ ⊃ SU(3)_color, φ is a
COLOR-sector operation. It is NOT Gresnigt's family S₃: by Brown's theorem Aut(𝕊)=G₂×S₃, and the
family S₃ is precisely the direct factor DISJOINT from G₂ (non-monomial) — used exactly so that
family ≠ color. This brick therefore does NOT connect the zero-divisor monomial-168 to fermion
generations, and does NOT amend Erratum E1 (which correctly places the monomial-168 inside G₂). It
reproduces the paper's octonion triple and exhibits the G₂/color realization of their 3-set
permutation — nothing more. A genuine bridge would require building the fermion ideals and showing
Brown's S₃ acts on those states as a monomial-168 element; that is not done here.

receiver holds the ADDRESS of the handle slot. lower.sio passed that address
straight into __sounio_seq_get / IrArrayLen, so the callee read one
indirection level off -- and the program still type-checked.

comments: This test used to be disabled, with the claim it checks written only as a
comment, because no surface syntax could produce IndepKnowledge. The type kind
existed in the checker and nothing could reach it. Now the grammar exists and
the test asserts against the compiler instead of describing what it would say.
Do not write the skip annotation in prose here: the harness matches that string
anywhere in the file, so mentioning it silently turns this test off.
A variable is never independent of itself: P(X, X) = P(X)·P(X) only in the
degenerate case. So `IndepKnowledge<f64, x, x>` asserts nothing — and asserting
nothing is exactly how an unfounded quadrature gets licensed, since the
composition law in stdlib/epistemic/graded_effects.sio grants the tighter
bound to any claim that type-checks.

this. No causal graph can be declared in source yet, so nothing can discharge
a well-formed claim. What the compiler enforces here is the one rule it can
know without a graph — and it enforces it rather than assuming it.
Reference: Pearl 1995, d-separation; Bayes Ball (Shachter 1998).

This is the Madaros half of a measured engine divergence. On main@88c2ab8ee8
the *mut checker spine calls checker_check_refinement_literal_inplace from
exactly two places (check.sio:9627, 9687), both in the let/var handlers, and
check/compat.sio never looks at refinement_id. So under Madaros a refinement

$ artifacts/madaros --check tests/compile-fail/refinement_f64_return_violation.sio
check: OK
lean_single rejects the same file. tests/known_failures/
hardened_diagnostics_full_suite.txt records the split in its own words
(2026-08-23): "default Madaros still answers `check: OK` on that file, so the
refinement is unenforced there; that is a compiler defect, not a manifest
one." This test is that defect, pinned for the integer case.
SCOPE. checker_check_refinement_literal_inplace only fires when
last_literal_kind is 1 (int) or 2 (float), so this pins the LITERAL return.
The propagated case is a separate, still-open hole:
fn lift(x: i64) -> { n: i64 | n >= 0 } { x }        // still accepted
fn f() -> { n: i64 | n >= 0 } { let b = 0 - 7  return b }  // still accepted
Those need dataflow the checker does not have here; main's own
tests/compile-fail/refinement_return_var.sio pins that case for lean_single
and is untouched by this test. Closing the literal case is what the
known-failures manifest asks for, and is where the fix stops.
The refinement is written INLINE, not through a `type` alias. A named alias
takes a different path on the *mut spine (checker_lower_named_type_mut does
not consult the refinement table) and fails with E008 "expected Fp, found
i64" long before the refinement is consulted -- a separate, unfixed defect
that this test deliberately does not depend on.
